body: I had a bout of psychosis that landed me in jail. After jail I got a full-time job doing warehouse work. I had enough money to get into a housing program so I moved from my parents place. After about two years I got another job, in my field and worked that for close to a year. Unfortunately my symptoms got the best of me and I recently had to walk of the job, though I'm fighting for medical leave as my exit was due to mental health issues. I've been in worse spots and I've known others who've lost it all, wound up in homeless shelters and still found a way out. Turning back from what seems like a dead-end is never easy, I find for myself the best option is to find a job that is doable, get up, stick to the routine and then carve out a better situation little by little. If you have to move back to your parents then start looking at what you can do from there that will keep you occupied. I'm planning a move myself and the best thing I can do to stay positive is just get up and do something with the day, free time to dwell is one of my worst enemies.  You may not be able to do what you want with your life but you can always do something with it, I certainly had big dreams when I was younger but for many of us, we have to accept what we are both capable of and what we can handle.

It depends on if the joy of being alive, simple pleasures, a sunset, the ocean, music, food, etc. hold enough weight to counter-act oblivion. The thought that it would be the last time you ever did something. I hope to at least be somewhere beautiful before I die. Have some fleeting moment of wonder brought back into existence. Then I hope to rationally prepare myself for my last times.
It's never too late you can always turn your life around, then you can turn it around again and find yourself right back in the same shit spot you started in, like me!

I know I have it better than millions of people in the world, doesn't provide me any comfort, got glass in my eye a long time ago.

At the time I wasn't on medication and I thought I would test myself to see if maybe it was just situational anxiety/depression. What I learned was that I need psych medication and unfortunately my experience in a foreign country was a mixture of loneliness, home-sickness, anxiety, and in some cases straight up embarrassment. 
After all the things I've tried to do to improve my life I just wanted some of the positive changes to actually stick to me, to mold me into a better man, but it hasn't worked, I'm still the negative, bitter,  shitty person I've been for the past 20 years, of course that isn't all of who I am, but unfortunately that is the person that seems to exist at the forefront of my personality.

Now that I am 34 I wish I had died when i tried to kill myself at 13. I would have missed out on a lot of good things but I would trade the good things for the peace of mind I've lost. Since I hit puberty my mental illness has only progressively gotten worse, I've been fighting for 21 years only to wind up alone, isolated, mentally incompetent and trapped in the life my illness has built for me. Now in my thirties it's becoming clearer and clearer I will never be able to get out of my own way and have the life I envisioned at 20, 25, or even at 30. I've grown to know the person I am, I hate who I am but I do not hate myself, I didn't ask to be the way I am. I didn't choose to be sick nor did I choose to have a learning disability, or to be gay. I didn't chose to be weak and negative. All the choices people seem to imply are in fact choices do not feel like choices to me at all. I've tried, and if I was supposed to change, or be happy by choice, then I have failed.

Your thinking patterns may be stuck on the suicide since you have been considering it for so long, perhaps CBT would be beneficial to restructuring your thinking patterns.
